video_title: If Bitcoin Hits This Price, the Supercycle Is Dead
gist: Strive CEO Matt Cole explains how the Bitcoin-only treasury company scaled to 40,000+ BTC via its SATA and fixed-15% SATS preferreds, why STRC de-pegged (levered TradFi retail liquidations), and why he underwrites a 'forever short on the dollar' with a ~50% BTC CAGR target through 2030 — while saying a fall to $40,000 would invalidate his supercycle view.

insights.claim: Strive grew from about 5,000 BTC to roughly 40,000+ BTC in a year, launching two Bitcoin-backed preferreds (SATA and SATS) and becoming the second issuer of digital credit after Strategy.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Strive is now a meaningful corporate BTC buyer and the main alternative to Strategy in the digital-credit market.

insights.claim: Strive deliberately launched its treasury strategy Bitcoin-only with no debt or convertible notes, using a reverse-merger shelf and ATM to position for quick preferred equity issuance; peers carrying convertibles were largely locked out of digital credit during the bear market.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Capital structure (absence of converts) determined which treasury companies could keep raising in the bear market.
insights.quote: we turned down all debt. We turned down convertible notes. And we basically launched a treasury company with Bitcoin only and nothing else

insights.claim: Strive runs an 'amplification ratio' of about 65% — far above Strategy's — and Bitcoin falling actually helped it raise that ratio; surviving the bear market convinced investors higher ratios were sustainable, letting SATS launch at 60-70% amplification.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Strive common (ASST) offers higher beta to Bitcoin than MSTR; its preferreds pay higher yields as compensation.
insights.quote: we now have an amplification ratio of about 65%.

insights.claim: Having a live preferred gives the issuer proprietary demand data from investors, which directly led Strive to design SATS; Cole sees this information advantage compounding.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: First-mover issuers in digital credit gain product-design edge over latecomers.

insights.claim: Strive holds about $50 million of Strategy's STRC on a $3 billion+ balance sheet as a liquidity buffer between cash and Bitcoin, but investors punished the position so it has not been increased.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Cross-holding of peer digital credit is a liquidity-management tool the market has not yet rewarded.

insights.claim: Cole believes Strive's common stock, though at a premium to Bitcoin NAV on an EV basis, trades at a discount on a discounted-cash-flow basis under any Bitcoin bull thesis.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: CEO signals he views ASST as undervalued vs. forward Bitcoin-amplified cash flows.

insights.claim: Strive is willing to sell Bitcoin (and could even sell BTC to buy back stock), but won't near-term because it would damage digital-credit investors' faith in the balance sheet; its goal is maximizing common-equity total return, not BTC count, and S&P has never asked it to sell.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Low near-term risk of Strive being a BTC seller; protecting the preferred franchise is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: if we saw an opportunity to not harm the digital credit business, enhance shareholder value, would we sell Bitcoin? Yes, we would.

insights.claim: Vivek Ramaswamy, Strive's founder, now owns roughly 5% of the company after accretive dilution and has effectively no involvement beyond being a mentor and large shareholder.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Key-person/political-brand association with Strive is fading.

themes.theme: Preferred market structure and the STRC de-peg

insights.claim: Strive's first SATA offering at $125 million drew 'no bid' from several institutions because it was too small; upsizing to $200 million made it more oversubscribed — institutions cap exposure at ~5-10% of an issue and need size to matter.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Small digital-credit launches struggle; scale itself unlocks institutional demand.
insights.quote: at 125 million, several institutions said no bid. And they said no bid because it was too small for them.

insights.claim: Institutions are capped on per-issuer exposure, so Strategy cannot be winner-take-all in digital credit; buyers need multiple issuers even of near-identical products.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Room for several digital-credit issuers; contradicts retail view that Strategy monopolizes the category.

insights.claim: Cole attributes STRC's fall below par to traditional-finance retail investors who over-levered on STRC via brokerages (not DeFi), then were force-liquidated as brokerages raised margin requirements, leaving a ~$1-2 billion hole in demand.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Explains why Strategy had to buy back STRC aggressively; leveraged demand likely won't return soon.
insights.quote: I think a lot of people thought it was DeFi but I actually think it was traditional finance oriented.

insights.claim: SATA held about $10 better than STRC at the lows because brokerages allowed less leverage on the smaller SATA, though short interest in SATA spiked as traders shorted SATA versus long STRC; both are now back near par.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Pair-trade dynamics link digital-credit prices; watch short interest and margin policy.

insights.claim: Cole expects leverage to rebuild and get flushed periodically when volatility gets too low, but less severely now that investors have been burnt; he argues holders for even a few months have essentially always had positive total returns.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Digital credit will retain episodic drawdown risk; not zero-volatility instruments.

insights.claim: Structured Bitcoin finance is working as designed: common equity (ASST) is more volatile than Bitcoin while preferreds like SATA are substantially less volatile, though not volatility-free.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Investors can choose risk along the Bitcoin capital stack.

themes.theme: SATS fixed 15% and the perpetual dollar short

insights.claim: SATS pays a fixed 15% dividend forever and is junior to SATA; it was created because the most common investor objection was not Bitcoin risk but fear that variable yields on SATA/STRC would fall to 7-8% as they succeed.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Investors wanting to lock in high yield now have a fixed-rate perpetual option; Strive gains issuance flexibility with no price protections.

insights.claim: Cole frames selling fixed 15% perpetual preferred as a 'forever short on the dollar', underwriting a perpetual Bitcoin bull thesis centered on a US dollar debt crisis.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Strive's equity is a levered bet on dollar debasement; if BTC CAGR stays low the 15% coupon becomes a burden.
insights.quote: It's a perpetual short on the dollar. It's not a fiveyear short on the dollar. It's a forever short on the dollar.

insights.claim: Cole argues AI is deflationary and will accelerate the US debt crisis: falling costs of food, transport and healthcare reduce money velocity and tax receipts while the debt load remains, increasing demand for scarce assets like Bitcoin, real estate and sports teams.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Non-obvious link: AI deflation is bullish for scarce assets via fiscal stress.
insights.quote: our view is that AI is actually going to be an accelerator of the debt crisis.

insights.claim: Cole notes the 10-year Treasury yield rose for 40 years (1940-1980) and fell for 40 (1980-2020), and expects it to grind higher for 20-40 years due to the debt crisis, implying dollar failure in roughly 15-35 years.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Bearish long-duration Treasuries over a multi-decade horizon.

insights.claim: Strive discounts the Bitcoin power-law model because it assumes decelerating returns; Cole instead expects an S-curve where Bitcoin re-accelerates as fiat debases, citing gold's history of calm years followed by violent rips.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Argues against the consensus that BTC returns must mature and dampen.
insights.quote: What you'll find with gold is that it has periods where it's calm for quite a few years and then it just has violent rips upwards.

insights.claim: If Bitcoin were only around $100k in five years, Cole says Strive's common equity would be roughly flat but it could still meet all dividend obligations.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Gives a downside-scenario anchor for ASST and coverage of preferred dividends.

themes.theme: Who buys digital credit and why

insights.claim: SATS' order book was roughly one-third long-term institutions, one-third fast-money institutions and one-third retail; SATA's typical buyer is a high-net-worth retiree with $1-10 million seeking income.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Buyer base is income-seeking HNW capital, a new demand channel for Bitcoin that doesn't come from existing holders.

insights.claim: Cole says he has never met anyone who sold Bitcoin to buy SATA or SATS; digital credit brings in bond and real-estate income investors who would never buy Bitcoin directly, creating net new Bitcoin demand.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Rebuts the Bitcoiner critique that digital credit cannibalizes spot demand.

insights.claim: Cole contrasts digital credit's four-month recovery to par with TLT's negative five-year total return, arguing income investors judge drawdowns against bonds and real estate, not against perfect par stability.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Digital credit's volatility looks acceptable relative to the long-duration Treasury experience.
insights.quote: the US Treasury ETF, TLT, it has a negative total return over the last 5 years.

insights.claim: Drawing on 16 years at CalPERS managing ~$70 billion, Cole says institutional mandates typically require a ~3-year track record and positions of ~$1 billion+, so institutional demand for digital credit should ramp over years 3-10.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Expect a step-up in institutional digital-credit demand starting around 2027-28 as products age.
insights.quote: at year three you start to see a pickup of institutional demand but it's probably like years 3 through 10

insights.claim: Investment-policy mandates block many institutional Bitcoiners from buying BTC or ETFs; wrappers like equities (Strive's largest holder is an active Fidelity equity fund) and future asset-backed securities with senior/junior tranches holding preferreds can unlock billions to low trillions of demand.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Product wrapping is the mechanism for structural institutional Bitcoin demand; watch for Bitcoin-preferred ABS.

insights.claim: Cole personally owns no digital credit, only Bitcoin and 'amplified Bitcoin' (Strive common), and argues digital credit yields outpace fiat debasement while bonds don't and forward S&P 500 returns look challenging.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: CEO's own positioning signals maximum conviction in equity, not the preferreds.

insights.claim: Cole views digital credit as a transitional asset for a 10-35 year move toward a Bitcoin-denominated future, but is pessimistic Congress will ever grant a de minimis capital-gains exemption for spending Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Bitcoin-as-payments policy upside is unlikely; savings use case dominates.

insights.claim: Cole's supercycle definition allows 30-50% drawdowns but not 80%; if Bitcoin falls to $40,000 he would consider the supercycle theory failed.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Clear invalidation level for the supercycle thesis.
insights.quote: if this ages poorly and we go to 40,000, then I would say that that theory did not play out.

insights.claim: Cole argues net buying by corporate treasuries like Strategy (a couple hundred thousand BTC) and Strive (40,000 BTC) dampened this bear market's downside and will amplify the upside once price recovers to $80-100k.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Treasury-company flows are a key swing factor in BTC volatility.

insights.claim: Strive targets a ~50% Bitcoin CAGR through 2030 (low case ~30%, high ~70%), contingent on liquidity conditions and Bitcoin reclaiming its role as a faster horse than gold; reaching $500k-$1M would require a real liquidity injection, which Cole sees as likely.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Explicit return target that underpins Strive's 15% perpetual coupon economics.
insights.quote: we have call it by the end of 2030 50% Kagger target.

insights.claim: Cole sees weak demand for long-dated Treasuries and upward yield pressure as 'springtime' for a Bitcoin bull market, and dismisses one or two possible Fed hikes as not materially changing that.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Monitor long-end auction demand as a leading indicator for Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Cole notes gold topped and bottomed before Bitcoin, and says if Bitcoin can't keep pace with gold it has 'kind of failed' as a thesis; he expects it to outperform.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: BTC/gold ratio is a key tracking metric for the debasement trade.
insights.quote: Bitcoin should be the fastest horse amongst the scarce assets.

insights.claim: Cole sees AI-enabled hacking as a major industry risk, likely hitting hot wallets and exchanges with small-scale hacks, but not institutional cold storage where Strive's Bitcoin is held; he says the industry oversold how easy self-custody is.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Security incidents may favor regulated institutional custodians over self-custody near term.

insights.claim: Cole says DOGE's rapid failure to cut spending (with Vivek and Elon involved) reinforced Strive's conviction that dollar debasement will never stop.
insights.speaker: Matt Cole (CEO, Strive)
insights.so_what: Fiscal restraint is the one thing Cole says would slow Bitcoin's growth; its absence supports the debasement trade.
